Cloud Migration of Electronic Health Records (EHR) System

A HIPAA-compliant, zero-data-loss transition strategy to modernize St. Jude Metropolitan Hospital's clinical data infrastructure for high availability, interoperability, and long-term cost efficiency.

1. Background & Current State

St. Jude Metropolitan Hospital operates a 450-bed acute care facility, three outpatient specialty clinics, and a regional diagnostic center serving over 280,000 active patients. Currently, our core Electronic Health Records (EHR) platform, clinical document repository, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) run on legacy on-premises servers housed in a primary hospital data closet and a secondary colocation site.

Installed in 2018, this infrastructure is approaching hardware end-of-support in Q4 2027 and faces critical operational, clinical, and security pressures:

  • Reliability & Clinical Downtime: Over the past 12 months, the hospital experienced 19.5 hours of unplanned EHR degradation or downtime due to storage controller bottlenecks and patch-window outages, forcing clinicians onto paper-charting contingency workflows.
  • Escalating Capital & Maintenance Costs: Refreshing the aging SAN storage arrays and virtualization hosts on-premises would require $1.15M in upfront hardware capital expenditure, plus rising annual maintenance renewals for 85 TB of rapidly growing imaging and clinical records.
  • Interoperability Bottlenecks: Legacy firewall topologies and batch-based HL7 v2 interfaces limit real-time data exchange with telehealth platforms, regional health information exchanges (HIEs), and patient mobile portals via modern HL7 FHIR R4 APIs.
  • Cybersecurity & Disaster Recovery Exposure: While compliant with baseline HIPAA controls, our current backup architecture yields a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 12 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 4 hours—insufficient against modern healthcare ransomware threats and regional power disruptions.

Migrating the patient records ecosystem to a HIPAA-eligible, HITRUST CSF-certified cloud environment (under a signed Business Associate Agreement) eliminates imminent hardware refresh debt while establishing a resilient, scalable clinical foundation.

2. Project Objectives & Success Metrics

The overarching goal of this initiative is to transition St. Jude Metropolitan Hospital's patient record workloads to a multi-zone cloud architecture safely, predictably, and without compromising active patient care. Success will be measured against six quantifiable objectives:

High Availability & Disaster Recovery

Achieve 99.99% clinical application availability (<53 minutes unplanned downtime/year) across active-active availability zones, reducing Disaster Recovery RTO from 12 hours to ≤15 minutes and RPO from 4 hours to zero data loss (synchronous replication) for transactional EHR records.

Clinical Performance & Workflow Speed

Reduce average chart-load and longitudinal history query times by at least 35% (<1.2 seconds p95 response time) during peak morning rounding hours, directly saving physician and nursing documentation time.

Security, Privacy & Regulatory Compliance

Enforce end-to-end Zero Trust security compliant with HIPAA, HITECH, 21st Century Cures Act, and HITRUST CSF v11, including FIPS 140-3 customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), immutable air-gapped backups, and automated PHI audit logging.

Interoperability & Financial Sustainability

Deploy a managed HL7 FHIR R4 API gateway for seamless HIE, lab, and patient portal integration, while lowering 5-year Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) by an estimated 24% ($1.08M net savings) compared to an on-premises hardware refresh.

3. Project Scope

To maintain strict governance over schedule and budget, project boundaries have been clearly established between in-scope migration deliverables and excluded adjacent systems.

In Scope

  • Core EHR & Clinical Databases: Full migration of inpatient, outpatient, emergency department, pharmacy, and order-entry modules (~14 TB structured relational data, 1.4M historical and active patient records).
  • Medical Imaging & Unstructured Records: Tiered cloud migration of 71 TB of PACS DICOM studies, scanned consent forms, and pathology PDFs (hot tier for <24-month studies; instant-retrieval archive tier for older records).
  • Cloud Landing Zone & Network Connectivity: Redundant 10 Gbps private dedicated cloud interconnects from the main hospital campus, HIPAA security guardrails, SIEM logging, and Single Sign-On (SSO) + MFA federation.
  • Clinical Integration Engine: Re-platforming 42 active HL7 v2, DICOM, and FHIR R4 interfaces (labs, radiology modalities, e-prescribing, billing feed, and regional HIE).
  • Validation, Training & Legacy Decommissioning: End-to-end clinical UAT, dress-rehearsal cutovers, super-user training for 1,100 clinical/administrative staff, 60-day hypercare, and certified HIPAA media sanitization of retired servers.

Out of Scope

  • EHR Vendor Replacement: Re-platforming uses our existing EHR software suite upgraded to its cloud-native release; switching to a different EHR vendor is excluded.
  • Biomedical & Bedside Hardware Procurement: Replacement of physical bedside patient monitors, infusion pumps, or workstation-on-wheels (WoW) fleet hardware.
  • Non-Clinical ERP Systems: Hospital payroll, general ledger finance, and HR human-capital systems (scheduled under a separate FY2028 administrative IT roadmap).
  • Paper Chart Digitization Backlogs: Pre-2010 physical microfiche and off-site paper archives not currently indexed in the electronic document management system.

4. Phased Implementation Timeline

The migration follows a 9-month (36-week) structured healthcare methodology beginning January 11, 2027, and concluding September 17, 2027. Continuous background data seeding and two full mock cutovers ensure the live weekend cutover window requires less than 90 minutes of read-only mode.

7. Risk Register & Mitigations

Proactive clinical and cybersecurity risk management ensures patient safety remains uncompromised before, during, and after cutover:

Risk Event Severity Potential Impact Mitigation & Contingency Plan
Extended Cutover Downtime High Disruption to Emergency Department triage, inpatient medication administration, and lab order turnaround. Pre-seed 98% of data continuously; run two timed weekend Mock Cutovers (<90 min target); maintain local read-only clinical snapshot appliances on every unit; retain instant DNS rollback to legacy system if delta sync exceeds 120 minutes.
PHI Exposure or Misconfiguration During Transfer High HIPAA reportable breach, regulatory fines, and loss of patient trust. Transfer data exclusively over private TLS 1.3 encrypted 10 Gbps circuits (zero public internet exposure); enforce automated Policy-as-Code blocking public storage buckets; validate with independent penetration test prior to loading live PHI if needed, and enforce FIPS 140-3 CMEK at rest.
Legacy Clinical Interface Incompatibility Medium Delayed diagnostic lab results, radiology reports, or pharmacy dispense messages. Complete comprehensive 42-interface audit in Phase 1; deploy protocol-translating cloud integration engine supporting legacy MLLP/VPN tunnels; require joint vendor end-to-end attestation in Phase 4 UAT.
WAN / Hospital-to-Cloud Circuit Outage Medium Loss of hospital campus connectivity to cloud-hosted EHR applications. Provision dual physically diverse 10 Gbps carrier circuits entering separate hospital MPOEs with sub-second BGP failover, backed by an encrypted 1 Gbps SD-WAN cellular/broadband tertiary link.
Cloud Storage & Egress Cost Spikes Medium Annual cloud OpEx exceeding the $508,000 operational forecast due to PACS imaging growth. Configure automated S3/Blob lifecycle policies moving DICOM studies >24 months old to low-cost archive storage; negotiate cloud provider medical imaging egress waivers under enterprise agreement; enforce monthly FinOps budget alerts at 80% threshold.
Clinician Workflow Friction at Go-Live Low Slower charting throughput or increased help-desk ticket volume during Week 1. Preserve core clinician UI workflows (infrastructure + minor version upgrade rather than EHR replacement); deploy 65 trained floor super-users ("at-the-elbow" support) across day and night shifts for 14 days post-cutover.

8. Call to Action & Approval

Recommended Decision & Immediate Next Steps

To retire our aging on-premises storage arrays well ahead of their Q4 2027 end-of-support deadline—and avoid $1,150,000 in non-strategic hardware refresh capital—the Enterprise Health IT Office requests formal Board and Executive authorization of $1,388,000 in Year-1 project funding by December 11, 2026.

Upon sign-off, the project team will immediately execute the following 30-day mobilization actions:

  1. By December 18, 2026: Countersign the Cloud Service Provider Enterprise Agreement, HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA), and Migration Partner Statement of Work.
  2. By December 23, 2026: Place carrier orders for dual diverse 10 Gbps hospital-to-cloud private circuits (accounting for 45-day telecom lead times).
  3. By January 6, 2027: Convene the inaugural Clinical & Executive Steering Committee and onboard departmental physician/nursing super-user leads.
  4. January 11, 2027: Launch Phase 1 Discovery & HIPAA Security Risk Analysis Kickoff.
